title: Starting with any free option? Also setting up a workflow?
author: teofilattodibisanzio
selftext:
I'm extremely money challenged but in would like to try and put together some ideas I've had for years... 

I made a few mockups that run on HTML of the games ideas but I would like them to shine and build a bit of workflow on I dunno unity? Rust? 

Not sure what would be the best options for either 2d or 3d results.

I'm totally open to all and any suggestions! Obviously  if you need any other infos to give me hints or suggestions let me know I'll gladly add details! 

Also in case it's really impossible to run something free to test the results, what would your suggestions be? 

Thanks a lot in advance!

replies.author: ImpressiveGooseHead
replies.body:
Sounds like you’re doing it! Honestly if you’re in there every day and solving problems and moving forward, you’re on the right track. 

The big deal imo is getting MCP connectors into blender and your game engine. I’m pretty sure Claude makes you be in the $20 plan for that, but you can also use LM studio and one of the smaller Qwen models locally too. They have ones that fit on 8gb pretty sure!

comments.author: GornoUmaethiVrurzu
comments.body: I keep it cheap by doing lots of the coding myself because I know how to code. So for example I did the character controller partially me, partially Claude and Copilot. Those two gave me animation importing and rendering and some of the complicated math stuff. Then I programmed the actual movement because it's get the math hooked up. Then I send it through Claude occasionally to let it clean things up and make them more intuitive. I'm not a professional or anything, just self taught over the last decade or so. My code isn't amazing. So Claude cleans it up nicely. I learned blender a few weeks ago and had Claude make an export script to use Blender as a level editor. Now I level edit in blender. I make models for the environment is 10-15 minutes because it's a PS1-Wii style game with simple geometry and low rest art. Characters are a lot harder because of animations and making them unique. But props? A complete breeze now that I've been doing this for a few weeks. Make an asset>put it in a level>ctrl+s is scripted to auto export it to my game>my game loads it. Boom extremely fast and easy pipeline on free models. I also wrote most of my engine with tutorials. You don't need to write an engine though. But I like keeping such a lightweight project with clean, directed AI code and easy to make human code. I've made my current project hundreds of times faster than before. It's incredible. Good luck 👌

replies.author: GornoUmaethiVrurzu
replies.body: The first barrier of getting to understanding it is usually the hardest. If you can get the basics down, you'll be way better than the vibe coders who can't look at their own code and understand anything at all. The basics are just understanding data types and how code is structured to run as an algorithm. Tutorials and tell AI to teach you have made it easier than ever. You're on a very privileged position to learn should you try.
